column1: Notes & assumptions
1. Failure modes, sub units, maintainable items and % values are transcribed from the OREDA compressor images in this folder.
2. Only failure mode / maintainable item combinations with a non-zero % are listed. % = share of total compressor failure rate.
Each row = one failure mechanism + one resolution. The % is repeated on every row of the same mode/item pair for filtering;
totals use column J (1 = first row of the pair) so the % is counted once.
3. Small totals differences vs OREDA 'Sum' column are due to rounding in the source tables.
4. Sub unit allocation follows OREDA Table 5. An item listed under several sub units in Table 5 is paired with EVERY one of them:
Instruments -> Power transmission, Compressor unit, Control and monitoring, Lubrication system, Shaft seal system;
Valves -> Compressor unit, Control and monitoring, Lubrication system, Shaft seal system, Miscellaneous;
Seals -> Power transmission, Lubrication system; Cooler(s) -> Lubrication system, Miscellaneous;
Filter(s) -> Lubrication system, Shaft seal system; Piping ('Valves & piping' / 'Piping') -> Compressor unit, Lubrication system, Miscellaneous;
Reservoir w/heating system -> Lubrication system, Shaft seal system ('Reservoir').
OREDA gives ONE % per failure mode/item (not split by sub unit), so the same % is shown under each sub unit but counted once.
Valves outside the Compressor unit use a separate mechanism set (oil/seal gas/control/utility valves instead of compressor valves).
Items not in Table 5 were assigned by judgement: check valves / internal piping -> Compressor unit; control-, isolating & check valves
-> Control and monitoring; couplings -> Power transmission; lube oil / oil tank -> Lubrication system; pipe supports -> Miscellaneous.
Instruments = OREDA instrument types flow, general, level, pressure, speed, temperature and vibration merged into one item;
its % is the sum of the types and its mechanisms are the union of the type-specific mechanisms (type named in the detail).
5. OREDA placeholder items 'Other', 'Subunit' and 'Unknown' (failure not traced to a specific item) are excluded, so there is no
'Unspecified' sub unit. They account for 13.96% of the OREDA failure rate, so the listed total is 85.66% (not ~100%).
6. Failure mechanism names are taken from the OREDA failure mechanism list (file 'failure mechanism.jpg'). For each maintainable
item only the mechanisms from that list that are physically relevant to the item were selected (sheet 'Mechanism Library'),
each with an item-specific detail (column G), the failure modes it can cause, and one or more resolutions.
A mechanism appears on a Failure Hierarchy row only when it can cause that failure mode for that item.
Structure is one-to-many: 1 failure mode/item -> many mechanisms -> many resolutions; each mechanism x resolution is its own row.
Failure mode 'OTH - Other' maps to mechanism 'Other' and 'UNK - Unknown' maps to 'Unknown' for every item.
7. Resolution names are taken from the OREDA resolution list (file 'resolution.jpg'); the specific action is in column H.
Each failure mechanism gets every resolution judged plausible for it (sheet 'Resolution Matrix', 233 of 37 x 13 pairs);
implausible pairs (e.g. Wear -> No Fault Found, Open circuit -> Overhaul, Fatigue -> Service) are excluded. One row per resolution.
Column H gives the action: 'Item-specific' (column K) = action from the item mechanism library; 'Standard' = generic action
for that resolution. Item actions whose resolution fell outside the matrix were moved to the nearest allowed resolution.
8. Mechanism selection/detail and resolutions are engineering judgement and should be reviewed against site CMMS history / RCA
before use in RCM or FMEA.
